comparators.minimum_variance: SLSQP on the joint scenario covariance; duplicate/singular tickets handled under constraints
comparators.probability_weighted: S allocated in proportion to combined ticket probability

mel.constraints: SLSQP; sum(stakes) = S; 0 <= stake <= S/2 (single ticket: S); positive wealth
mel.objective: maximise sum(scenario probability * log(A + scenario net . stakes))
mel.q_formula: q = clamp(pc + cohort_shift, 0.001, 0.999); cohort = market group x 10-point pc band
mel.scenarios: binary pre-match win/loss over unique legs; cross-fixture conditional independence; exact shared legs reused once; probabilities sum to one
mel.stress: simultaneous q - 0.05 re-solve; descriptive, not a bound
mel.ticket_net: odds - 1 on a win, -1 on a loss

protocol.evidence_rule: at least N* settled playable rounds and the whole-round bootstrap lower 95% bound on mean log growth above zero
protocol.inconclusive_rule: report inconclusive after 156 settled playable rounds without the evidence rule
protocol.n_star_rule: ceil(((z_0.95 + z_0.80) * sd(round log growth) / log(1.02))**2)
protocol.n_star_unavailable: report N* unavailable rather than invent a value
protocol.stop_adaptive_rule: upper 95% estimate of losing 50% within 52 rounds above 5%, or the owner's loss budget is breached

research_note: Existing audits are hypothesis generation, not an untouched holdout. No retrospective fair-odds substitution is used in actual-price results.

settlement.round_atomic: bankroll, peak and drawdown advance once after every available ticket in a round is terminal
settlement.rules: any lost leg 0; all legs void 1; mixed landed/void the product of actual prices for landed legs only
settlement.unresolved_exposure: the whole round stake is reserved until then

fallback_labels: below meaningful payout floor; highest available payout
ticket_construction.overlap: soft non-overlap across best2/around3/around5; relaxation is recorded
ticket_construction.ranking: combined pc, model_EV, fewer legs, log-distance to target, deterministic identity

version_rule: Any formula, parameter, scenario or stopping-rule change creates a new version and a new forward record.
